mission.cluster: one unified pairing and trust state machine for every join entry point: session phases and legal transitions, ephemeral key exchange bound to stable fingerprints, human-readable device preview with optional non-authoritative MAC evidence, one-time Owner confirmation with replay protection, expiry/cancel/reject/fail cleanup, trust roles as classifications rather than grants, credential rotation, revoke, lost-device revoke, quarantine and re-pair, reconnect revalidation, and an audit log that proves transitions without carrying key material

whyNoDonor: RF-002 is new Owner-defined construction, not a donor migration. There is no upstream file to port and therefore no donor commit to pin: writing a DONOR.json here would have to invent provenance. The manifest records `donor: null` for the same reason, and the city manifest test requires exactly that for a programme-task incubator.

cityPlacement.why: RF-001 already declared the City map's own building for this ownership: 00-foundation/02-city-node-network, 'City Node Network - Device Node Fabric', whose declared ownership is node/device principal identity plus membership and trust. RF-002 is the trust half of that building and belongs beside device-identity rather than in a building of its own, because a pairing cannot be understood apart from the identity it binds.
rejectedAlternatives: A separate building: rejected because the City map already assigns node identity and trust to one building, and splitting them would let the two drift.
08-device-edge: rejected for the same reason as RF-001 - that district is about physical sensor/actuator capability, not node trust.

provenanceForm.decision: Registered under the mission-book programme-task incubator id `mb-rf-002-pairing-trust-lab`, carrying this PROVENANCE.json and `donor: null`.
provenanceForm.why: Same honest form RF-001 established: no Room ever incubated this code, and it is not a migration, so neither the Room Pack identity nor the `mb-<MB-ID>` migration identity would be true.

knownBoundaries: No transport, discovery, Bluetooth or rendezvous implementation. RF-003..RF-005 own those; this module receives an entry point as data and never performs discovery itself, which is exactly what makes 'many join methods, one trust protocol' enforceable.
No transport encryption. Invariant 4 requires authenticated encryption on every path; this module establishes trust and binds fingerprints, but RF-006 owns the secure transport path manager.

No capability resolution, permission computation or task/action semantics. `capabilitiesFromTrustRole` always answers none, and `checkReconnect` returning `allowed: true` is explicitly not a permission.
No persistence. The authority is in-memory; a durable store and its reload semantics are not in this task's scope and are recorded as an integration seam.

No product or service consumer is wired in this component task. The natural seam is `services/dev-gateway/pairing.mjs` + `services/dev-gateway/discovery.mjs`, which today implement a descriptor/QR/short-code flow with no session state machine and no trust record. Recorded as an integration seam for the Remote merge workbook, per mission-book/CROSS_PROGRAMME_EXECUTION_CONTRACT.md section 5.
The audit log is bounded (2048 entries) and in-memory; a durable audit sink is RF-009 scope.

`checkReconnect` treats a rotated credential as a refusal. Whether a rotated credential should instead trigger an automatic re-pair is a policy decision for the Owner; this module refuses and names the reason (`credential_rotated`) rather than guessing.

acceptanceMapping.local discovery, Bluetooth and remote in: ENTRY_POINTS + startSession; every entry point creates the same session and walks the same PAIRING_TRANSITIONS
acceptanceMapping.two sides display stable fingerprints fo: exchangeEphemeralKeys binds both fingerprints; buildDevicePreview carries the responder fingerprint and confirmPairing re-checks it
acceptanceMapping.reused/expired pairing attempts are reje: seenChallenges replay guard (challenge_replayed), one-time confirmation_token_ref (confirmation_replayed), lazy expiry (session_expired) and cleanupExpired
acceptanceMapping.trust role changes are explicit and audi: changeTrustRole records from/to in the trust history and the audit log
acceptanceMapping.MAC mismatch may warn but cannot replace: buildDevicePreview.mac_evidence.mismatch_warning plus MAC_AUTHORITY = NOT_AUTHORITY and trustFromMacEvidence always refusing
acceptanceMapping.logs prove state transitions without lea: auditLog records state transitions; auditLeakScan proves no PEM block or named secret appears
